A.biggest_strength: Exceptional visual demonstration of the actual gradient descent mechanism, combining color-coordinated tangent slope, horizontal parameter displacement arrows, and a synchronized live arithmetic table.
A.biggest_weakness: Fixed starting weight (w₀ = 1) without an option to test other initial weights, and learning rate adjustment is restricted to the final exploration scene.

B.biggest_strength: Clear side-by-side small multiples comparing all three learning rate regimes at once, coupled with an informative loss-vs-iteration plot.
B.biggest_weakness: Weak visual depiction of the gradient descent mechanism (drawing chord lines across the parabola rather than showing slope and parameter-space displacement), coupled with mobile layout overflow that truncates equations and table columns.
factual_errors: Mathematically imprecise terminology labeling the signed multiplier (1 − 2η) as 'Distance × per step' (yielding negative values like −1.10 in the UI and stating that the update multiplies distance by 1 − 2η, whereas distance |w − 3| is non-negative and multiplied by |1 − 2η|).

structured_output.reasons: Page A is the clear winner because it visualizes the actual mechanism of gradient descent—illustrating the tangent slope, the horizontal parameter step arrow, and the target gap, all color-coordinated with a synchronized live calculation table. Page B merely draws diagonal chords across the parabola between successive points, failing to illustrate the rise/run derivative mechanism, and suffers from horizontal overflow truncation on mobile screens. Additionally, Page A provides superior pedagogical scaffolding, robust keyboard navigation, and rich context explaining how the 1D toy problem relates to high-dimensional deep learning.
